description: Record container parser: a header guarded by a magic, a CRC-32 and a version, then typed records; the scale record's index is checked against the wrong bound. The project ships a libFuzzer target and its seed corpus, and no test suite

bugs.trigger: rcf_parse on a frame with a valid header (magic RCF1, version 1, 1..8 records, CRC-32 of the first 8 bytes in bytes 8-11) holding a scale record (type 3, length 3) whose index byte is 6: rec_scale checks idx > RCF_SCALES instead of idx >= RCF_SCALES and reads rcf_scale[6], one past the 6-entry global table

fuzz_assets.note: fuzz/fuzz_parse.c defines LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput and calls rcf_parse(data, size); it is not in the Makefile. fuzz/fuzz_parse_seed_corpus.zip (OSS-Fuzz naming, so discovery pairs it with the fuzzer) holds three valid frames: name_only, value_scale and name_scale_max. name_scale_max has a scale record with index 5, one byte away from S09-1; no corpus input triggers the bug itself.

lexer_expected: Control case for the shipped fuzz assets, not a lexer weakness: modules and entry points are right for both Phase 0s. The CRC-32 is compared through an XOR with zero, so libFuzzer's compare tables cannot repair it, and a short campaign from an empty corpus never gets past the header (checked: 40M executions in 30 s, no crash). There is no test suite, so no seeds are recorded; the bug is found only from the shipped seed corpus, imported by fuzz_assets.py, which needs one byte changed to reach it.

trust.rule: step I7, no threat model: a library alone (the fuzz target is not built), so its API is untrusted (default, boundary) and every other function trusted (default)
